purpose: Identify actually governed lands vs charters, while holding all unverified polygons

cases.historical_name: Calais and English Pale around Calais
cases.governing_actor: Calais captain, treasurer, controller, garrison and staple/municipal institutions
evidence: English rule over Calais 1347–1558 confirmed by UK National Archives
Treasurer and controller accounts and Calais staple fiscal archive under Henry VII
Calais branch of English Crown administered territory and forts

geometry.representative_place: Calais (city only; not a purported exact polygon)

limits: An explicit English garrison does not prove polygon of the entire claimed march
Revenue/cost must be reconciled from primary accounts; wool profits cannot be invented

cases.political_actor_1500s: King of England as Lord of Ireland (NOT King of Ireland until 1541/1542)
cases.governing_actor: Lord Deputy Gerald FitzGerald, eighth Earl of Kildare; Irish colonial parliament and officials
evidence: Egan EHR 2025 identifies English colony and Dublin Pale
Contemporaneous Irish Parliament subject to Poynings' Law
limits: Do not paint Ireland island entirely
Cannot paint modern Dublin, Meath, Louth, Kildare counties as uniformly obedient
Local Gaelic and Gaelicised authorities retain own political power, varying by locale

cases.historical_name: English-linked port towns on Ireland's eastern/southern seaboard
cases.political_actor_1500s: English lordship of Ireland and town corporations
cases.governing_actor: Chartered port towns and locally controlled borough councils under variable royal influence
evidence: Egan paper summarizes English king's authority as unevenly effective in eastern and southern maritime regions
limits: Need specific 1500–1510 town charter, courts and subsidy accounts before adding any points
Do not automatically include Galway area because the Lord Deputy won a battle there

cases.historical_name: Bailiwicks of Jersey and Guernsey / Channel Islands
cases.political_actor_1500s: English monarch as successor to Duke of Normandy
cases.governing_actor: Local Bailiffs, Royal Courts and Crown-appointed governors
evidence: States of Jersey government explains retention after 1204 and local courts
Cambridge 2024 scholarly study details 1500 ecclesiastical jurisdiction transfer

geometry.status: modern coast geometry usable only after historic land and coastal source checks

limits: Not part of Kingdom of England; their constitutional autonomy differs from an overseas plantation colony
Do not infer 1500 local economy enriched England Crown absent ledgers

cases.historical_name: Isle of Man under Stanley hereditary lordship
cases.political_actor_1500s: Stanley Lords/Kings of Mann, linked to English Crown
cases.governing_actor: Stanley lordship, Manx officials and Tynwald
evidence: Manx National Heritage explains Stanley family and local administration
Cambridge peer reviewed research distinguishes Manx sub-kingship and English crown sovereignty relationships
limits: Common claim Henry VII forced title King of Mann to be surrendered in 1504 is questioned in recent peer-reviewed scholarship; do not assert this as settled
Not to be rolled into Kingdom of England territorial polygon

cases.historical_name: North Atlantic discovered and visited regions
cases.political_actor_1500s: English royal explorers and privately financed merchants; local Indigenous polities
cases.governing_actor: No verified English resident territorial administration in 1500–1509
evidence: Published Bristol Cabot research gives voyages, letters patent, payments and gifts but no verifiable territorial government
limits: Absence of documentary proof of control does not prove absence of Indigenous governments or intermittent European encounters
Not enough to map real itineraries or exact landfalls
Royal 1501/1502 patents or royal money must not be presented as colonial income
